brief: TS Lombard argues, via The Market Ear, that US homebuilder fundamentals are deteriorating beneath a still-stable technical range. XHB has traded in a range since 2024, and the latest bounce started near the range's lower end, but rising rates and weakening fundamentals raise the risk that support eventually breaks. XHB moves inversely with the 10-year Treasury yield. Operating margins have fallen below pre-Covid levels because median new-home prices are falling even as construction input costs rise 10-11% annually, squeezing builders from both sides. The NAHB buyer traffic index has dropped to 18, its weakest since the Covid recession, while mortgage rates near 7.3% keep affordability depressed. Inventories are rising even as starts and permits weaken, and builders are cutting construction activity in response. TS Lombard sees renewed upside risk to US yields as growth stays resilient and inflation persists, a risk compounded by hawkish Fed communication. TS Lombard expresses this bearish housing view through a relative-value trade: long the equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) versus short homebuilders (XHB) at a 1.75:1 ratio, targeting homebuilder underperformance rather than a broader market decline.
